The principles hold for research software in any programming language and
scientific field, whatever tools it uses. Most are general software engineering
principles, stated and motivated for a setting where the typical failure is not
a crash but a plausible, wrong number. A smaller set is specific to research
software, such as numerical stability, units and axis conventions, missing
values, and reproducibility.

[](design.qmd) is the main document. The guides to testing and to documenting
stand beside it, and the three form one set of guidelines, with the normative
language, the ladder, and the terminology of *Design Principles*.
[](test-types.qmd) defines the terms of testing for all of them. The languages
and the tools apply these principles and cite them.
